messages:
Mina: heads-up: ran into a flakey case in the sample streaming app where a short disconnect (~150-400ms) causes events to be merged or reorder on Windows. pretty consistent on win10 with node 18. anyone else?
Oscar: do you have logs and exact repro steps?
Mina: run sample-streaming, request a long (15s) streaming completion, then toggle wifi for ~200ms midway. client reconnects and sometimes emits: eventA+eventB combined, or eventB before eventA. parser shows 'partial delimiter' warnings.
Mina: log excerpt:
```
[sse-client] recv: "data: {\"chunk\": \"part1\"}\\n"
[sse-client] network down, reconnecting
[sse-client] recv: "data: {\"chunk\": \"part2\"}\\n\\ndata: {\"chunk\": \"part3\"}\\n"
[sse-client] emitted payload: {\"chunk\":\"part2part3\"}
```
Oscar: sounds like boundary detection is fragile when the separator (LF LF) gets split across TCP segments. Node and Python SDKs currently differ in parser approach, right?
Mina: yes — node uses a streaming stateful parser, python sample used a regex split on "\\n\\n" in earlier versions. python showed more merged events.
QA-bot: confirmed on CI: python 1.6.2 with regex split fails 70% of runs for this scenario, node 3.2.0 passes but sometimes reorders if resume header overlap occurs.
Infra-bot: proxy v2.4.3 has known behavior: when resuming with Last-Event-ID, proxy may replay a small suffix if upstream hasn't drained. scheduled audit created: https://git.internal/redwood/issues/6901
Oscar: two orthogonal bugs: 1) fragile client-side parsing, 2) proxy resume overlap. mitigation options: make parsers buffered/stateful (accumulate until full delimiter), normalize CR/LF combos, and add a monotonic X-Chunk-Seq header so clients can detect out-of-order/dupe.
Mina: I prototyped a minimal change in python sample: buffer += chunk; while True: idx = buffer.find(b"\\n\\n"); if idx==-1: break; evt = buffer[:idx]; buffer = buffer[idx+2:]; handle(evt) — fixed merge in my tests.
Oscar: good. for node we should also normalize CRLF variations before searching for delimiter, e.g., replace(\\r\\n, \\n) and consider retaining partial bytes at reconnect.
Mina: i also hit a Windows-specific case where CR and LF arrive in separate recv calls and the regex loses the separator. normalization or stateful scanning fixes that.
Oscar: infra suggestion: add a tiny jitter (50-200ms) before sending Last-Event-ID on resume so proxies can finish draining, or better, make proxy avoid replaying already-sent suffix.
Infra-bot: filed proxy follow-up: https://git.internal/redwood/issues/6902 (avoid replay overlap on resume).
Mina: opened PR for python sample + test: https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/3501 (buffered parser + unit that simulates 1-4 byte splits across boundary).
Oscar: i'll add a small node sample patch to normalize CRLF and include a flaky-streams e2e that toggles link for 100-300ms on Windows runner. please add a note in sample README saying naive regex is fragile.
CLI-bot: PR 3501 opened by mina in repos/sample-python (labels: devex, flaky-streams).
Mina: follow-ups assigned: infra to audit proxy resume, platform to consider X-Chunk-Seq header, sdk teams to adopt buffered parsers and add Windows e2e.
Oscar: agree. long-term we should ship an opt-in X-Chunk-Seq or event_id in payload so clients can dedupe deterministically. quick wins: buffered parsing + CRLF normalization + small resume jitter.
Mina: thanks all, will post CI results here after Windows e2e runs. :thumbsup:
